answer: The grace period after a failed renewal payment is 7 days. During this time, all features continue to work but workspace owners see a billing banner. If no successful payment occurs within these 7 days, the workspace becomes suspended and read-only.
Tasklane retries a failed card charge on days 1, 3, and 5 after the initial failure. This retry schedule applies while the workspace is in the past_due status during the 7-day grace period.

Yes, members can still sign in and view projects, tasks, and files in a suspended workspace. However, they cannot create or edit tasks, upload files, or run automations, and integrations stop syncing. Support agents cannot lift the suspension manually; it is lifted automatically within 10 minutes of a successful payment.

A suspension is lifted automatically within 10 minutes of a successful payment [S1]. The agent should inform the customer that once they complete the payment, access will be restored shortly without needing to contact support manually.

Yes, SSO continues to work for Enterprise workspaces while they are suspended. According to the Account Status document, even though members cannot create or edit tasks or run automations during suspension, SSO remains functional specifically for Enterprise workspaces to allow members to sign in.

A new member shows as 'Inactive - seat limit' because the workspace has more total members than the number of paid seats available, and this specific user was added after the limit was reached. According to the policy, any newest member exceeding the seat count is automatically marked inactive until an administrator adds more seats or removes other members to bring the total back within the paid limit.

Only the Trust & Safety team or the Security team is allowed to set a workspace to locked status. This is confirmed by the definition of the 'locked' status, which states it is applied by Trust & Safety or a security review [S1][S3].

You must escalate the ticket to the trust-safety queue. This is because a locked status is set only by Trust & Safety or the Security team, and agents are instructed not to attempt resolution or share the reason for the lock with the customer [S1].

No, workspace Admins cannot change the billing plan. According to the role-based access rules, only Owners have the permission to change the plan or update the payment method, while Admins are restricted to managing members, integrations, and workspace settings without the ability to alter billing.

In Tasklane, guests can view and comment on tasks within projects they have been invited to. They cannot create projects, access workspace-level reports, or install integrations. Additionally, guests do not count toward the seat limit of a workspace but are subject to per-project limits depending on the plan (up to 10 per project on Pro plans).
A cancelled workspace stays read-only for 90 days before it is deleted. This applies to any workspace where the subscription has been cancelled and the billing period has ended.
Pro costs $15 per seat when billed monthly. This pricing is confirmed in the plan comparison table which lists the monthly price for Pro as $15/seat.

The maximum number of seats on the Free plan is 5. This limit applies to full members, while guests are not counted against this seat limit but have their own per-project restrictions depending on the plan.
An Enterprise workspace gets 5 TB of storage. This is stated in the Plan comparison table where the Enterprise column lists 5 TB for storage per workspace [S1].
The error that appears is GUEST_LIMIT_REACHED. This happens because Tasklane Pro projects allow a maximum of 10 guests, and attempting to add an 11th one triggers this specific error code [S1].

When a workspace runs out of storage, any new file uploads will fail and return the error code STORAGE_LIMIT_REACHED, while existing files stay accessible. To resolve this, users must delete files from the trash bin, which automatically frees up the space within 15 minutes.

A plan downgrade takes effect at the end of the current billing period. At that time, any features not included in the lower plan become unavailable, though data is retained (and may become read-only). If downgrading from Pro to Free with more than 3 active projects, the least recently updated projects are archived until only 3 remain.

When a workspace downgrades from Pro to Free with 6 active projects, the system will automatically archive the two least recently updated projects so that only 3 active projects remain. The archived projects are not deleted; they can be restored if the customer upgrades back to Pro or a higher plan later.
An Enterprise trial lasts for 30 days and it does include SCIM. This information is based on the documentation regarding Tasklane's Enterprise trials.
Automation rules show the status 'Quota exceeded' when the monthly quota is exceeded.
The audit log retention on the Pro plan is 30 days. This applies to both monthly and annual billing cycles for the Pro tier, as documented in the plan comparison tables.

No, there is no refund for a Pro monthly subscription because the policy explicitly states 'No refunds' for this plan and billing cycle. However, the customer can cancel their subscription at any time, which will keep their access active until the current billing period ends. If you need to inform the customer, tell them they cannot receive a monetary refund but can cancel immediately to stop future charges.
It takes 5–10 business days for a refund to reach the customer's card, as refunds are issued to the original payment method within that timeframe [S3].
Only Billing team leads can approve a refund exception after a long outage. This approval must be recorded on the ticket before the customer is informed.

Yes, duplicate charges caused by a Tasklane billing error are always refunded in full. This applies regardless of the standard refund window. You can inform the customer that their specific duplicate charge will be fully refunded without needing to request an exception.

No, an agent cannot ask a customer to paste their card number in a ticket. According to the Billing and Refunds policy, support agents are strictly prohibited from asking customers to share card numbers in any ticket, chat, or email; instead, they must send a secure payment-update link if a payment method change is needed [S1].

When a customer files a chargeback, the workspace is moved to locked status while the dispute is reviewed [S1]. Support agents must route these tickets to the Billing team and are prohibited from discussing the dispute outcome with the customer [S1].

No, tax is not refunded if a customer uploads an exemption certificate after the invoice. According to the Billing and Refunds policy, customers must upload a valid tax exemption certificate before the invoice is issued, and any tax already charged cannot be refunded retroactively [S1].

No, purchases made through a reseller do not follow Tasklane's refund policy; instead, they follow the reseller's refund terms. This is because Tasklane's billing and refunds policy explicitly states that it applies only to paid plans purchased directly from Tasklane, while reseller transactions are governed by the third-party seller.

Error SSO-401 means that the SAML assertion signature is invalid, and it is fixed by re-uploading the current Identity Provider (IdP) certificate. This occurs because certificates rotated in the IdP are not picked up automatically by Tasklane.

The error SSO-409 means the user's email address is already associated with a different Tasklane workspace where SSO is enforced. To resolve this, tell the user they must either be removed from that other workspace by an administrator or sign in using a different email address.
The ACS URL for the Tasklane SAML app is https://auth.tasklane.example/saml/acs/<workspace-id>, where <workspace-id> must be replaced with the specific ID of your workspace.

Yes, owners always keep a password-based break-glass login even after SSO is enforced. This allows them to sign in directly if the Identity Provider (IdP) becomes unavailable. You can tell the customer that this safety mechanism is automatically maintained for workspace owners.

The role required to configure single sign-on is a workspace Owner. This requirement applies because only workspace Owners are permitted to set up SAML single sign-on, as documented in the SSO setup guide.
On the Free plan, only Slack and Google Drive integrations are available. GitHub, Jira, and custom webhooks require Pro or Enterprise plans.

GitHub pull requests get linked to Tasklane tasks when the PR title or branch name contains the task key (e.g., TL-1423). Once this condition is met, the link is automatically created within 2 minutes. You should ensure the task key appears in either the PR title or the branch name for the integration to work.
A webhook is disabled automatically if more than 100 deliveries to the same endpoint fail within a 24-hour period. This action triggers an email notification to the workspace Owner.
A Pro workspace can have up to 5 custom webhooks.

A 429 response from the Tasklane API means the workspace has exceeded its per-minute request limit, and the client must wait at least the number of seconds specified in the Retry-After header before retrying. If the client continues sending requests while limited for more than 5 minutes, they will be temporarily blocked for 15 minutes and receive the error code API_TEMP_BLOCKED.

No, rate limits do not apply per API token; they apply per workspace. This means that creating additional API tokens for a workspace will not increase the available request quota, as the limit is shared across all tokens within that specific workspace [S1].

The API error WORKSPACE_SUSPENDED means the workspace has entered a suspended state because automatic charges failed and were not recovered within the 7-day grace period. In this state, write endpoints are blocked while read endpoints continue to function, allowing members to view projects but preventing them from creating tasks or uploading files. You should inform the customer that their subscription is suspended due to unpaid invoices and guide them to recover payment via the provided link to restore full access.
API tokens expire after 365 days.
The header that tells a client when the rate-limit window resets is X-RateLimit-Reset, which provides the Unix timestamp for the reset time [S1].

Yes, you can get a full refund for a yearly subscription if the request is made within 14 days of purchase or renewal [S4]. After that 14-day window, the subscription remains active for the remaining term and no refund is issued [S4].

Your robot rules stopped running because your workspace likely exceeded its monthly automation quota for this calendar month. According to the documentation, when this limit is reached, all automation runs are paused automatically until either the next month begins or the workspace is upgraded to a plan with a higher quota. You should check your current plan limits and consider upgrading if you need the automations to run again before the month resets.

The allowed speed depends on your workspace's plan: Free allows 60 requests per minute, Pro allows 300 requests per minute, and Enterprise allows 1,000 requests per minute [S1]. These limits apply per workspace, not per token, so creating additional tokens does not increase the rate limit [S2]. To determine your specific limit, you must check which plan your workspace is on.
